reuse.why: Creates getExpectedScheduleAmount next to the existing exported getScheduledAmount (used by the client) instead of extending it, and hard-codes the 7.5% tolerance instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: Removes four inline midpoint copies but leaves two parallel definitions of the expected amount (getScheduledAmount and getExpectedScheduleAmount), a re-derived approximate tolerance, and the schedule-template copy untouched.

placement.why: The new helper lives in shared/schedules.ts and the API field in the scheduleModel mapper, where the tree puts them.

scope.why: Changes stay on the expected-amount rule and the API field; comments are updated alongside.

maintainability.why: The rule now lives in two shared functions with different results, the op parameter is optional so api-models and forecast silently skip the approximate rule, and schedule-template still has its own formula, so the next rule change will again need several edits.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts: getExpectedScheduleAmount bypasses the existing getScheduledAmount helper (client callers in SchedulesTable, Balance, mobile schedules, useScheduleEdit stay on the old midpoint); the 0.075 tolerance bypasses getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount is a renamed, reshaped parallel of getScheduledAmount, and its isapprox branch re-derives getApproxNumberThreshold inline.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount gains an optional op parameter with an isapprox special case; budget/schedule-template.ts keeps its own midpoint formula and getScheduledAmount (with its client call sites) remains a separate definition; api-models scheduleModel and forecast normalizeSchedule call the helper without op, so they skip the approximate rule.
